title: Registered Hytale 360 panoramas with generated landscape and immutable protected pixels
summary: Build explorable spherical concepts from calibrated native captures, share a distant environment across viewpoints, and composite generated near terrain only inside explicit image masks. Pixel preservation and viewer validation do not establish a shared 3D scene or a completed game-world build.
problem_class: registered spherical environmental simulation with protected source imagery
problem_description: Generate coherent 360-degree landscape proposals around an existing playable map while preserving the observed buildings, crops, paths and orientation, and distinguish rendered proposals from actual world geometry.
context: Zytale, Windows, Hytale 0.7.2 revision d769dc3d57881261a62858e1394f0e4de9a21eca. Three elevated coordinate viewpoints, night captures plus supplemental fullbright inspection. User approved the first distant landscape and later the three near-terrain simulations.
inputs: Ten calibrated native captures per viewpoint: eight horizontal headings plus zenith/nadir
Near-terrain allow polygons and protected exclusions
outputs: Standalone three-viewpoint HTML with original comparison
Masks, prompts and scoped validation reports
constraints: Keep protected source pixels exact outside the permitted near-terrain mask
Do not equate raster masks with authoritative playable-volume boundaries
Do not equate generated new tree/rock positions with shared 3D geometry
Keep historical and current viewer tests distinct
Respect a user stop or browser security rejection; do not bypass it
known_attempts: Calibrated native projection plus distant-only background
Prompt-guided near-terrain generation followed by exact masked restoration

solution_versions.description: Project actual native captures onto a calibrated sphere, preserve map foreground and composite a common distant environmental image, then expose three viewpoints and original-image comparison in a standalone WebGL viewer.
changes: Verify north=-Z, east=+X and heading=-yaw modulo 360 against native compass and installed Transform.getDirection
Use eight horizontal captures plus up/down at observed vertical FOV 90; exclude window borders
Use one shared coordinate-based distant backdrop instead of independently inventing three horizons
Keep original source panoramas for comparison and scene protection
advantages: Preserves actual map composition and direction
Supports 360x180 exploration with no external runtime assets
Shared backdrop preserves the broad orientation of distant features
disadvantages: Raster backgrounds cannot establish actual terrain depth or engine feasibility
Landmark positions and 1.7-block optical offset are approximate
test_results: Original viewer: 23 functional checks passed in headless Edge 155.0.4283.45 with software WebGL
Reported frame timing from software WebGL is not a Hytale performance benchmark

solution_versions.description: Extend the registered panoramas into unused near terrain using explicit allow masks, protected holes and inside-only feathering; restore the original base everywhere else. Deliver the three viewpoints with comparison and display-only brightness control.
changes: Use the first approved landscape as the shared distant base; keep the later hidden-summit revision historical
Give ImageGen the clean panorama, a permission overlay and cross-view references
Resize generated raster to the source projection, match exposure and feather the edit only inside each allowed mask
Restore exact base pixels outside the mask, then inspect rectilinear projections and record hashes
Distinguish three independent visual concepts from a shared exact 3D build
advantages: Protects buildings, crops and paths at the pixel level despite global changes in raw generator output
Allows near-environment integration while retaining original captures and previous versions
Makes limitations and actual validation explicit
disadvantages: Allowed terrain was selected visually in 2D; game-space protection requires an independent 3D audit
Individual new trees/rocks may differ across viewpoints
New viewer not freshly tested interactively in browser
test_results: Changed pixels inside allowed masks: 955199, 511328, 483812; outside: 0,0,0
Twelve rectilinear final views and six base comparisons checked visually
Six embedded 4096x2048 images matched SHA-256; JavaScript syntax and unique control IDs checked
Rendering/texture logic and pointer/keyboard code matched previous tested viewer after label normalization
Final 17-file ZIP: 44628012 bytes, CRC32 and every contained SHA-256 checked
User described result as very close to excellence and requested recording in Forge/GitHub

metrics.reliability: Exact protected-image comparison passed for all three views
metrics.performance: No actual Hytale landscape performance test; nothing built in the world during this visual phase
metrics.compatibility: Standalone WebGL viewer; fresh browser interactive verification remains outstanding

transferability: Direct reuse of ray projection, inside-only feathered masks, lossless source preservation and evidence separation for similar panoramas. Analogy to multi-view concept validation in other engines; native camera conventions, world APIs and playable bounds require fresh verification.

metrics.reliability: Zero pixels changed outside allowed near-terrain masks in all three final PNGs; validated only for this raster artifact workflow.
metrics.compatibility: Observed Hytale 0.7.2; no implied compatibility of world editing APIs.
